title: Minecraft’s official system requirements have updated for the first time in 17 years
summary: Mojang has updated Minecraft: Java Edition's official system requirements for the first time in 17 years, increasing minimum and recommended specs to reflect modern hardware needs. The changes call for more memory, stronger processors, and graphics hardware supporting Vulkan 1.3. The update aims to ensure playable frame rates on common presets at 1080p, without signaling a massive graphical overhaul.
content:
How many games do you know that update their system requirements 17 years after they came out? Given how long Minecraft has thrived for almost two decades now, it's probably not a surprise that the game requires beefier hardware today than it did on launch. Mojang has updated its aging system requirements for the game, and honestly, the new requirements are very reasonable given how the game has evolved.

Over on the Minecraft website, Mojang has announced a tweak to the game's system requirements. This is usually bad news for gamers who are concerned that their hardware is getting left behind, but don't panic. This isn't Mojang announcing a huge graphical rework that will leave thousands of older PCs unable to play Minecraft, but is instead the company updating the specs to reflect what the game really needs in this day and age:

The previous system requirements for Minecraft: Java Edition were based on older hardware and older graphics technology. While those specs may have reflected what Minecraft needed in the past, they no longer represent what the game needs to run well today.

This is why we’re raising both the minimum and recommended system requirements for Minecraft: Java Edition. The new requirements include more memory, more powerful processors, and graphics hardware that supports Vulkan 1.3.

The Minecraft team wanted to ensure that if someone booted up the game and picked the Fast graphical preset, they should get 30FPS at a 1080p resolution at an absolute minimum. As such, the minimum requirements are now:

This is less because Minecraft is getting a huge graphical update and more because the old system requirements didn't really reflect what the game was like anymore. As someone who loves playing on heavily-modded servers, I can attest that 8 GB of RAM is really cutting it close with Minecraft these days, so it was well worth tweaking the requirements to reflect reality.
